title: Permissions, MCP and context economy
summary: Grants stay local, a deny floor protects history, hooks are anchored, MCP stays local, and sessions close with /done instead of compacting.
why: Settings decide what Claude may do without asking and what every session pays in context; these defaults remove prompts for safe commands while refusing the few that destroy work, even under bypass.

items.title: Tracked settings hold hooks/env; permissions stay local
items.does: Adds a rule that the tracked project settings hold hooks, safe env values and deny rules only, and gitignores the local settings file that holds permission mode and allow lists.
items.why: A permission grant in tracked settings travels to every clone and every collaborator; keeping grants local means each person decides their own, while hooks and denies still apply to all.

items.title: Narrow allow list instead of bypass
items.does: Adds a local allow list for read-only and verification commands (git status, log and diff, the test runners, CI status); everything else still asks first.
items.why: It removes most permission prompts without granting arbitrary execution, which is the trade a bypass mode does not offer.
items.notes: Shown as inactive while bypass permissions is on: bypass skips the allow list, not the deny list.

items.title: Deny list for history-destroying commands
items.does: Adds deny rules to the tracked project settings for commit --amend, push --force and --tags, reset --hard and rm -rf of the repo root or its .git folder; deny rules hold even when bypass permissions is on.
items.why: Every one of these commands has destroyed work at least once, and an empty deny list stops none of them; a deny rule grants nothing, so it is safe to track and share.
items.notes: Prefix rules cannot catch every spelling of a command; the git hooks and lessons back the floor up.

items.title: Headless permission floor per run kind
items.does: Adds a file that gives each kind of unattended run its own floor: code runs accept edits with a fixed tool list, responders get read-only tools, planners run in plan mode; no kind ever gets a skip-permissions flag.
items.why: A read-only run that can still write a file the test runner later executes is not read-only; when bypass is set for the user, an explicit tool list per run is the only real floor.
items.notes: Enable later: with the headless module, so each kind of unattended run gets only the tools it needs.

items.title: MCP config local and gitignored; no OAuth server on a critical path
items.does: Gitignores the project MCP config and adds a rule: re-wire steps live in the README, no OAuth-gated server sits on a path unattended runs depend on, and headless runs use a strict MCP config.
items.why: A fresh clone silently lacked an MCP server it needed, and an expired OAuth grant stalled unattended runs; a local config with written re-wire steps and no OAuth dependency avoids both.

items.title: Close the session at ~70% context instead of auto-compaction
items.does: Adds a rule: at about 70 percent context, run /done and /clear instead of letting the session compact itself; a transcript over 10 MB is a warning, over 20 MB urgent.
items.why: Compaction summaries dropped carried items without saying so; the hand-off written by /done is the only continuity that keeps every open item.

items.title: Hook commands anchored to the project dir
items.does: Adds a rule that every hook command starts from an absolute anchor such as the project-folder variable, never a path relative to the current folder.
items.why: After a cd into a subfolder a relative hook path stopped resolving, and because a failing PreToolUse hook blocks every tool, both shells were locked out.
items.notes: Canonical text for the lesson lsn-anchored-hooks.

items.title: Text-first guard for screen-scrape tools
items.does: Adds a PreToolUse hook that denies the first screenshot, screen-scrape or clipboard tool call of a session with a reminder to read the same content as text first; a second call goes through.
items.why: A screenshot costs far more context than the text it shows, and most of the time the same content is reachable as a file, an API or page text.
items.notes: Enable later: if you use desktop-automation or screenshot MCP servers and want text tried first.

items.title: Chat answer token cap
items.does: Adds a rule that a chat answer stays under about 500 tokens, with detail written to a file the answer names.
items.why: Long chat answers buried the results the reader was looking for; a hard cap is a stricter version of quiet chat.
items.notes: Enable later: if answers still run long with quiet chat and the compressed output style on.
